The other three SQL 160 functions read the same ACL in both databases. SQL 160 does not name SQL 161 and is not changed by it; SQL 161 runs before SQL 160 in staging by the order of work. The file refuses a missing function (42883 sql161_function_missing) or role (42704 sql161_role_missing); the engine requires the function to exist and be owned by the applying login (acl_functions_present, acl_functions_owned_by_login) and to hold no EXECUTE entry other than PUBLIC, checksops and the owner, each granted by the owner (acl_functions_acl_replaceable; revokes []). The post-conditions require the body, attributes and owner unchanged (acl_functions_otherwise_unchanged). Production already holds the grant, so it is expected to read as already in the intended state (release sql161 v1: b916bcb512896ba7a90ac4401ad1903b18482d27e3173e8ccef21112eb4506f8, the intended fingerprint): the file is a no-op there and a pin whose expected live hash equals the intended one cannot be bound (INVALID_MANIFEST), as SQL 131's staging pin. Staging's expected pre-state (PUBLIC and the owner, each granted by the owner) is 72031400264a910912cecd832ac0bf8486da7b67acfd036bc66aff6820258448 (releaseStateHash('sql161', the intended state with that ACL)); its own read-live records it. No table, trigger, policy, body or other grant change; no API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin. Adds no trigger.
